p-runs

elements.el: Project chips with counts
elements.reason: All, then each project the last 24 hours ran, the most runs first, each a link that keeps the rest of the filter; the counts are the window's (RUNS_WINDOW_TEXT under the strip says so), while the list pages through the whole history

elements.el: Closed lists: Outcome, Reason, Flow, Trigger, Host, Venue, Forge and Model
elements.reason: each a labelled select in a plain GET form that Apply sends, so a filtered view is a link and needs no script: the outcome and forge lists are closed in code, the others offer the values the last 24 hours' runs carry and the one the query holds; a trigger reads as its row number

elements.el: A repository as its own field
elements.reason: the old filter form's repository field, kept: the card folds it into its search, and the console keeps the repository exactly (repo) beside the search's part of a target or a job id

elements.el: One search pill for a repository, target or job id
elements.reason: q matches a case-insensitive part of the target or the job id, at most 200 characters, a run id's own bound, so a repository's name finds its targets and any run id finds its run

elements.el: Applied filters as removable chips, with Clear filters
elements.reason: each chip's remove is a link to the page without that filter

elements.el: The summary strip counts the window by outcome
elements.reason: the five outcomes, each in its status's tone (completed in the ok tone), and the runs of an outcome this release does not know when there are any, counted and not linked; "at least" where the window is a floor

elements.el: Each count is a link that filters to it
elements.reason: the chosen project kept, the rest of the filter dropped

elements.el: 27 runs ended
elements.reason: the window's total is the All chip's count; the strip counts by outcome

elements.el: $6.13 metered spend
elements.reason: the window's settled spend from the run records (the chosen project's), with how many runs settled no amount where some did not; beside the switch under the strip

elements.el: Window: 24 hours, in the title bar and as an applied chip
elements.reason: the list pages through the whole history, 50 a page, so it has no window to choose; the project chips and the summary count the last 24 hours, and the line under the strip says so

elements.el: The summary when the last 24 hours could not be read
elements.reason: a state the card does not draw; where only one side of the window was read the counts are floors and RUNS_WINDOW_PARTIAL says so

elements.el: Completed runs are quiet: a grey badge and no sentence
Failed, refused, awaiting-input and cancelled runs carry their tone badge and a reason sentence with the shared prefixes
elements.shows: This repository's or folder's run cap for the window was already
elements.reason: awaiting input and cancelled say why in their own word, so their rows draw the badge alone; a failed or refused run's sentence is its reason's short catalog form without the verdict its badge already says, linked to every run with the same outcome and reason

elements.el: A run whose record names no reason
elements.reason: a row the card does not draw: an older worker's record, or a reason that is no record token, whose text is shown to nobody in either role

elements.el: Only problems switches the table to those rows
elements.reason: a link (problems=1) in the All outcomes and Only problems switch under the strip, rather than in the table's head, so the switched view is a link like any filter; it keeps every run whose word is not completed: a refused, failed or cancelled run, a run awaiting input (whose record says completed) and an outcome this release does not know

elements.el: Rows are grouped by day
elements.reason: by UTC day, each said as its date and UTC ("2026-10-08 UTC"), and runs whose record names no instant under RUNS_DAY_UNKNOWN

elements.el: Times are UTC
elements.reason: the Ended cell is the UTC time alone under its day's row, as the card writes it, the whole instant in the element's datetime (the date and the zone on every row made the cell 179 px for the card's 69); the browser script shows it in the reader's own zone with the UTC time in its title, alone where the reader's date is the row's UTC date and with the reader's date where it is not, by its data-day mark, which says the row names its day (a time without the mark always gains the reader's date); the day groups are UTC days and say so

elements.el: The table's head: 27 runs, newest first, times UTC
elements.reason: the history is paged, so the head counts nothing: the foot says how many rows the page shows, and each time says its zone

elements.el: A scheduled run's Job named by its trigger (tidy)
elements.reason: the cell shows the run's whole id, the one its run page opens; the trigger is the Trigger list's value

elements.el: Newer runs and Older runs
elements.reason: the page goes back through the history by a cursor, so its way forward is Newest, which opens the newest page again

elements.el: Showing 27 of 27 in the last 24 hours, 50 per page
elements.reason: the foot counts the page's rows; the history is paged through, not counted, so no total of it is shown

elements.el: When it ended, job id, target and forge link, flow, host, venue, outcome, model, tokens and job cap
elements.reason: the columns the runs table had; the project rides in the target's cell; flow, venue, model, tokens and job cap are marked hide-phone, head and cells, and a desktop narrower than the card's own 1,440 px leaves them out as a phone does (runs-css.mjs RUNS_TABLE.allMin), since with every column the table scrolled sideways by 136 px in a 1,280 px window; on a desktop every cell but the outcome's and the target's stays on one line, as the card draws it, a job id past 22 characters and a host, a flow or a model past 20 (runs-css.mjs RUNS_TABLE.valueMaxCh, the .val box) breaking inside a box of its own, so a long value grows its own row and never the table
